name = "EMAIL"
allowed_sender_addresses = ["no-reply@my.admin.news"]

# Workers AI: drafts the reason an editor gives when turning down a
# contributed article (src/lib/server/contributions/rejection-draft.ts, model
# openai/gpt-6-luna at xhigh effort). Built into every account, so there is
# nothing to create; usage is billed to the account. Under `wrangler dev` it
# calls the real service (needs `wrangler login`), and a failed call only
# shows an error on the rejection form.
[ai]
binding = "AI"

# Weekly R2 snapshot — Sunday 02:00 UTC. Feed refresh (followed feeds, watched
# MVP blogs, Message Center) and the AI review of new posts run hourly on the
# hour; podcasts sync in the 16:00 UTC run. Sponsor housekeeping (waitlist
# holds, ad reminders) and MVP feed discovery run hourly at :30.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Production deploy, used by .github/workflows/deploy.yml after
# scripts/rehearse.sh has passed and the deploy is approved. Runnable by hand
# from app/ with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID set (or after
# `wrangler login`); run scripts/rehearse.sh first.
#
#   1. Check pending D1 migrations (drizzle/ and drizzle-feeds/): refuse the
#      seed and unmarked destructive SQL (src/lib/deploy/migration-guard.ts).
#   2. Back up the main database if it has migrations waiting, then apply them.
#      The live code keeps working on the new schema (AGENTS.md).
#   3. Run pending deploy tasks in deploy/tasks/ (see deploy/README.md).
#   4. Build (with scripts/assets-ignore.mjs, which keeps the Worker's source
#      map out of the public assets) and upload the new version without
#      sending it any traffic, smoke-test it on its own version URL, then
#      switch all traffic to it, apply routes, crons and the queue consumer,
#      and smoke-test the live hosts. A failed check before the switch leaves
#      the old version live.
#   5. Run pending post-deploy tasks (*.post.sh).
#
# DRY_RUN=true lists what would happen and runs `wrangler deploy --dry-run`,
# changing nothing. D1_TARGET=--local points every D1 step at the local
# database instead and skips step 4, for trying tasks out.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
# shellcheck source=scripts/deploy-lib.sh
. scripts/deploy-lib.sh

DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-false}"
D1_TARGET="${D1_TARGET:---remote}"
BACKUP_DIR="${BACKUP_DIR:-.wrangler/deploy-backups}"
GIT_SHA="${GITHUB_SHA:-$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)}"
ADMIN_URL="${ADMIN_URL:-https://my.admin.news}"
SPONSOR_URL="${SPONSOR_URL:-https://sponsors.admin.news}"
MCP_URL="${MCP_URL:-https://mcp.admin.news}"

dry() { [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; }

# ---- 1 + 2. Migrations ---------------------------------------------------
# Check every database before applying anything, so a refused migration in
# one never leaves the other half-migrated.
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
for pair in $DATABASES; do
	db="${pair%%:*}"
	step "Checking migrations for $db"
	read_applied "$WORK/$db.applied.json" "$db" "$D1_TARGET"
	check_pending "$WORK/$db" "${pair#*:}" "$WORK/$db.applied.json" "${D1_TARGET#--}"
	if [ -s "$WORK/$db" ]; then
		printf 'Pending:\n%s\n' "$(cat "$WORK/$db")"
	else
		echo "Up to date."
	fi
done

for pair in $DATABASES; do
	db="${pair%%:*}"
	[ -s "$WORK/$db" ] || continue
	if dry; then
		echo "(dry run) would apply the pending migrations for $db"
		continue
	fi
	if [ "$db" = "newsletter" ] && [ "$D1_TARGET" = "--remote" ]; then
		mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"
		backup="$BACKUP_DIR/$db-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).sql"
		step "Backing up $db to $backup"
		wrangler d1 export "$db" --remote --output="$backup"
	fi
	step "Applying migrations for $db"
	wrangler d1 migrations apply "$db" "$D1_TARGET"
done

# ---- 3 + 5. Deploy tasks ---------------------------------------------------
# Exit status: 0 = already ran, 1 = not yet. Any other failure stops the
# deploy, so a lookup error can never make a task run twice.
task_done() {
	local out
	if out="$(wrangler d1 execute newsletter "$D1_TARGET" --json \
		--command "SELECT name FROM deploy_tasks WHERE name = '$1'" 2>/dev/null)"; then
		jq -e '.[0].results | length > 0' >/dev/null <<<"$out"
		return
	fi
	# Before migration 0046 is applied (dry runs only) nothing has run yet.
	if dry && grep -q "no such table: deploy_tasks" <<<"$out"; then return 1; fi
	echo "Could not check deploy task $1:" >&2
	echo "$out" >&2
	exit 1
}

run_tasks() {
	local phase="$1" f name
	shopt -s nullglob
	for f in deploy/tasks/*.sh; do
		name="$(basename "$f")"
		case "$name" in
			*.post.sh) [ "$phase" = "post" ] || continue ;;
			*) [ "$phase" = "pre" ] || continue ;;
		esac
		if [[ ! "$name" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then
			echo "Task file name must use only letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-': $name" >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		if task_done "$name"; then
			echo "Already ran: $name"
			continue
		fi
		if dry; then
			echo "(dry run) would run: $name"
			continue
		fi
		step "Running deploy task $name"
		D1_TARGET="$D1_TARGET" GIT_SHA="$GIT_SHA" bash "$f"
		wrangler d1 execute newsletter "$D1_TARGET" \
			--command "INSERT INTO deploy_tasks (name, git_sha) VALUES ('$name', '$GIT_SHA')"
	done
}

step "Deploy tasks (before deploy)"
run_tasks pre

# ---- 4. Build, upload, check, switch -------------------------------------
step "Building"
pnpm exec vite build
# Before anything is uploaded: keeps _worker.js.map (the server's source) out
# of the public assets.
node scripts/assets-ignore.mjs
if [ "$D1_TARGET" != "--remote" ]; then
	echo "D1_TARGET=$D1_TARGET: skipping the Worker deploy"
	exit 0
fi
if dry; then
	step "Checking the Worker bundle"
	wrangler deploy --dry-run
	step "Deploy tasks (after deploy)"
	run_tasks post
	step "Done (dry run)"
	exit 0
fi

step "Uploading the new version (no traffic yet)"
WRANGLER_OUTPUT_FILE_PATH="$WORK/upload.ndjson" \
	wrangler versions upload --message "deploy ${GIT_SHA:0:7}"
version_id="$(jq -r 'select(.type == "version-upload") | .version_id // empty' "$WORK/upload.ndjson")"
version_url="$(jq -r 'select(.type == "version-upload") | .preview_url // empty' "$WORK/upload.ndjson")"
if [ -z "$version_id" ]; then
	echo "wrangler versions upload didn't report a version ID." >&2
	exit 1
fi
if [ -z "$version_url" ]; then
	echo "Cloudflare gave the new version no URL to test it on, so it isn't going live." >&2
	echo "Turn on Preview URLs for the newsletter Worker (Settings → Domains & Routes)," >&2
	echo "then run the deploy again. See deploy/README.md." >&2
	exit 1
fi

step "Smoke-testing version $version_id on $version_url"
SMOKE_LABEL="new version, before it takes traffic" node scripts/smoke-test.ts --admin "$version_url" || {
	echo "The new version failed its checks and isn't live; production is unchanged." >&2
	echo "Any migrations above stay applied, which the live code tolerates." >&2
	exit 1
}

step "Sending all traffic to version $version_id"
wrangler versions deploy "$version_id@100%" --yes --message "deploy ${GIT_SHA:0:7}"
step "Applying routes, crons and the queue consumer"
wrangler triggers deploy

step "Smoke-testing the live site"
SMOKE_LABEL="live site" node scripts/smoke-test.ts \
	--admin "$ADMIN_URL" --sponsor "$SPONSOR_URL" --mcp "$MCP_URL" || {
	echo "The new version is live but failing. Check \`pnpm exec wrangler tail\`, and roll" >&2
	echo "back with \`pnpm exec wrangler rollback\` if it's broken (deploy/README.md)." >&2
	exit 1
}

step "Deploy tasks (after deploy)"
run_tasks post

step "Done"

name: Deploy

# Deploys the console Worker (app/) to Cloudflare. Run by hand only: Actions →
# Deploy → Run workflow, on main. Merging to main never deploys by itself.
#
#   1. verify:   pnpm check and pnpm test.
#   2. rehearse: app/scripts/rehearse.sh tries the deploy on a throwaway copy
#                of the production databases and smoke-tests the new build.
#                Changes nothing in production. Its summary lists what the
#                deploy will do.
#   3. deploy:   waits for approval (required reviewers on the `production`
#                environment), then app/scripts/deploy.sh applies the
#                migrations, uploads the new version, smoke-tests it on its
#                own URL before it takes traffic, and switches traffic to it.
#
# Both scripts run the same way from a laptop. See app/deploy/README.md for
# setting up the Cloudflare token and the two environments.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      rehearse_only:
        description: 'Rehearse only: test against a copy of production, deploy nothing'
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

# One deploy at a time, in order. Never cancel one halfway through a migration.
concurrency:
  group: deploy-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Check and test
    # Production only ever runs main. Pick main in the "Use workflow from" menu.
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

content.text:
Yes, the newsletter repo has a Deploy workflow. It only runs when someone starts it. It checks and tests the build, does a trial deploy on a throwaway copy of the production databases, and then waits for your approval before the real deploy. The last three runs, on Nov 2 and 3, all succeeded.

I tried to start it on `main`, but your Mac's auto mode blocked that as a production deploy too. To start it yourself:

1. Open the [Deploy workflow](https://github.com/merill/newsletter/actions/workflows/deploy.yml) and choose **Run workflow** on `main`.
2. Approve the deploy step when it asks.

The AI rejection drafts will still fail after the deploy until you add AI Gateway credits in Cloudflare.

The deploy failed at the test step, before anything went out, so production is unchanged. The fix is ready in [PR #96](https://github.com/merill/newsletter/pull/96). Merge it, then run the Deploy workflow again.

The cause is the two PRs together. #94 now refuses a submission from an author without a personal LinkedIn profile. The six new tests from #95 create a submission for a test author with no LinkedIn profile, so all six failed. Each PR passed its tests on its own, and the clash only showed once both were on `main`.

The fix is one line, in the test file only (no app code): it gives the test author a LinkedIn link. The full test suite passes locally, all 1,061 tests. I assigned the PR to you, asked you for review, and switched your local checkout back to `main`.

The AI rejection drafts will still fail after the deploy until you add AI Gateway credits in Cloudflare.

2. Add credits.
